messages.subject: IRT diferences in using callibrated itens and doing the callibration
parts:
Recently I applied a mathematics test for ensino fundamental (the Brazilian elementary school) composed by 24 items previously calibrated under a 3 parameters logistic model. The calibration of these items goes back to 2008, and all items used was fit for the curriculum. The parameters (A is the discrimination, B the difficulty parameter and C is the guess parameter) of each item is displayed as follows

            A      B      C
    0   0.000  0.000  0.000

    22  1.294  1.750  0.262
    23  1.244  0.922  0.249



There was 39 respondents and conditions of the calibration was reproduced (same test duration, same instructions and rules). Using mirt's function fscores to obtain the traits of each student, it resulted in a list whose mean is 169.6 (translated to the scale where the mean is 250 and sd 50 for pedagogical interpretations). This result was far away from the historical scores of the school.

After I used mirt and mirtCAT to calibrate and obtain the proficiency of the students. Using the generate.mirt_object I generated a mirt object and fscores to obtain the abilities. The result was a list of parameters (A is the discrimination, B the difficulty parameter and C is the guess parameter) displayed as follows

                A          B         C
    0   -0.908164  -0.888655  0.000011

    8   11.193242   8.704091  0.000020
    9    4.812878  -3.405279  0.211483
    10   0.851246  -0.472238  0.000014
    11   0.684467  -2.301309  0.172352
    12  18.404827 -37.285993  0.294857
    13   7.040281   0.902891  0.570133
    14  54.310470 -48.643073  0.328101
    15   0.380293  -0.020780  0.000125
    16   0.858722  -3.026284  0.128889
    17   0.634882   0.109751  0.000026
    18   0.644905  -0.001688  0.000015
    19  45.394522 -77.356946  0.383602
    20  58.895684 -52.991346  0.450317

    22  59.468859 -18.015848  0.359025
    23  45.549544 -77.591668  0.356788



and a list of abilities whose mean is 245.7 (translated to the scale where the mean is 250 and sd 50 for pedagogical interpretations). This result was consistent with the historical scores of these test in theses school. Also, the professors have confirmed the consistency of the data.

I'm new at IRT theory so I have no clue of what might have happened.

 1. What factors have to be ensured to use pre-calibrated itens in order to obtain the traits?
 2. These discrepancies is explained by the low number of respondents? 
 3. What could explain the assertivity of the second model for the traits?

messages.author: 69c6a0a9916b1351
messages.subject: Re: IRT diferences in using callibrated itens and doing the callibration
parts:
Hello Dr. Chalmers,
Thank you for the response. It follows the code that I used.

library(mirt)
library(mirtCAT)
test <- read.csv('test.csv') # the file containing the response
par <- read.csv('par_mt.csv') # file containing the parameters of each item
a1 <- c(par_mt[,3])
d <- c(par_mt[,4])
g <- c(par_mt[,5])
par_mt <- data.frame(a1,d,g)
mod_mt <- generate.mirt_object(parameters=par_mt,itemtype='3PL')
testresults <- fscores(mod_mt,full.scores=TRUE,response.pattern=test)

For the parameters of the first item I also find it strange, but it was on the official documentation of state of Sao Paulo's education department.
